messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High error rate detected on serving-runtime (us-west-2). Symptoms: CUDA OOM, CrashLoopBackOff, rapid pod restart churn. Paging infra-oncall.
infra-oncall: I'm on it. @sam (eng-runtime) @rachel (oncall-ml) joining. Current error spike: 12% 5xx, restart rate ~80/min across runtime pods.
sam (eng-runtime): attaching first logs — repeated `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB` immediately after pod startup. Pods get scheduled -> OOM -> node pressure -> autoscaler kicks in.
maria (sre): seeing node flaps too. Sequence looks like: autoscaler scales up quickly -> new pods schedule to new nodes -> pods OOM on first request due to bigger batch sizes being applied by runtime -> pods crash -> readiness probes fail -> autoscaler scales down because pod isn't Ready -> repeat. Looks like autoscaler cooldown is too short leading to oscillation (thrash).
alex (infra): pulled autoscaler config: scaleDownDelaySeconds=30, scaleUpStabilization=0, maxSurge=10. That is aggressive. I'll bump scaleDownDelay to 300 and set a minReplicas floor. Applying now.
eng-runtime: quick mitigation: temporarily pin routing to stable model variant with lower memory footprint and disable big-batch fusion. Plan: route 100% of traffic to redwood-base-8q (smaller) until we stabilize.
rachel (oncall-ml): +1 to model fallback. Initiating gradual reroute to redwood-base-8q at routing layer — will do 50% -> 100% if errors drop.
sam (eng-runtime): executing routing change: ```
# routing policy replace
route update serving-runtime --model redwood-base-8q --weight 50
```
ops-bot: routing update queued, canary at 50% applied.
maria (sre): also cordoning a few noisy nodes to prevent repeated scheduling while we fix pod runtime config. Commands: ```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-12-34
kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-34 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
```
sam (eng-runtime): rolling patch to revert to quantized-v1 runtime image (we suspect a regression in quantized-v2 memory allocator). Patching deployment now: ```
kubectl set image deployment/serving-runtime runtime=registry.redwood/serving-runtime:quantized-v1
```
infra-oncall: autoscaler damping rules updated (`scaleDownDelaySeconds=300`, `scaleUpStabilization=120`, set `minReplicas=8`). Also disabled aggressive burst scaling for this pool.
eng-runtime: after image revert + model fallback, OOMs dropped sharply. Error rate down from 12% -> 1.4% in 10 minutes. Pod restart rate normalized.
alex (infra): to prevent future thrash, adding a hysteresis policy: require node ready for 60s before counting towards scale down and increase eviction TTL. Will also add a cooldown metric to autoscaler using CPU+GPU utilization averages.
maria (sre): customer impact assessment in progress — current estimate: ~3% of requests in us-west experienced >1s latency spikes and ~0.8% transient errors during window. No data corruption. Top 5 customers on-prem/outbound webhooks notified by CSM.
eng-runtime: creating retrospective ticket: RUNTIME-2378. Root cause hypothesis: memory regression introduced in quantized-v2 combined with autoscaler aggressive defaults and runtime batch fusion creating large allocation on warm start.
rachel (oncall-ml): temp mitigation steps documented in the incident runbook: fallback model variant, pin runtime image, increase autoscaler cool downs, cordon noisy nodes.
infra-oncall: mitigation timestamp noted: 2075001680 (routing fallback + image revert applied). Monitoring for 30m.
ops-bot: incident channel created: #incident-2075001234; severity set to SEV2; incident doc: https://redwood.incidents/2075001234
liam (night-sre): taking handoff at 2075001800. I'll monitor overnight and follow up on the retro.
sam (eng-runtime): postmortem action items: 1) revert or fix memory allocator in quantized-v2 (owner: eng-runtime) 2) add autoscaler safety heuristics (owner: infra) 3) add canary gating for runtime images (owner: eng-platform) 4) add more granular telemetry for per-model memory use (owner: eng-ml).
maria (sre): assigning follow-ups in tracker and scheduling incident review. No more active throttling observed as of last check. Closing active pager. :white_check_mark:
infra-oncall: final recovery timestamp: 2075001889. Leaving notes in incident doc and pinging affected customer managers.
